source: Letter-associates cross-reference — Charles's company circle vs. the 153rd NY record
method: Read Charles's dispatches + the letters where he is discussed; extracted every named comrade/officer; cross-referenced each against the NY AG 153rd NY roster. Names tied to other brothers' regiments (Henry's 34th, Alexander's 60th) or to home were recorded as honest NULLs for the 153rd. Mirrors the Henry (Sweep 1.1) and Alexander (Sweep 2.0) method.
anchor_record: HUBBELL, CHARLES F.—Age 25; enlisted Aug 30 1862 at Champlain; corporal Co. I; mustered out Oct 2 1865, Savannah, Ga.
transcription_caution: The brother called 'Charles of the 60th' in LTR-1862-12-09-002 is ALEXANDER, not Charles. Charles's true Co. I circle comes from his own 1862-64 dispatches and James's letters.

confirmed_co_I_associates.verbatim_letter_context: 'James rec'd a flesh wound in the thigh or hip and walked about five miles to the hospital. Says James had made a bandage of his drawers.'
confirmed_co_I_associates.record_match: HUBBELL, JAMES.—Age 22; Co. I; mustered in Mar 9 1864; corporal May 1864; wounded Oct 19 1864 at Cedar Creek; mustered out Oct 2 1865.
confirmed_co_I_associates.fate_from_record: wounded Cedar Creek; survived to muster-out (died returning home 1865, post-roster)
confirmed_co_I_associates.note: Charles's brother; wound matches the letter exactly.

confirmed_co_I_associates.record_match: RICH, DAVIS J.—Age 31; captain Co. I, Oct 11 1862; discharged Nov 20 1863, Washington D.C.; also borne D. J. Rice; prior service as captain, 34th Infantry.
confirmed_co_I_associates.note: CROSS-BROTHER LINK: the same Davis J. Rich who commanded Henry's Co. D, 34th NY ('Capt. Reich', DSC-2026-06-05-002). Henry's captain → Charles's captain.

confirmed_co_I_associates.name_as_written: Lieut./Capt. McGuire ('our 1st Lieut. McGuire is a Catholic')
confirmed_co_I_associates.record_match: McGUIRE, JOHN F.—Age 24; 1st lieut. Co. I Oct 11 1862; captain Nov 21 1863 (vice D. J. Rich resigned); mustered out Oct 2 1865.
confirmed_co_I_associates.fate_from_record: rose to captain, succeeding Rich; survived
confirmed_co_I_associates.note: The officer who replaced Capt. Rich — binds the chain.

confirmed_co_I_associates.name_as_written: Lieut. Knapp ('called for Hubbell and Staats')
confirmed_co_I_associates.verbatim_letter_context: 'Lieut. Knapp ... called for Hubbell and Staats'
confirmed_co_I_associates.record_match: KNAPP, CHARLES L.—Age 21; 2nd lieut. Co. I Oct 11 1862; 1st lieut. Nov 20 1863; discharged May 28 1864 at Morganza, La.

confirmed_co_I_associates.name_as_written: James Lucas (tentmate; 'reduced for stealing rations'; reported only wounded)
confirmed_co_I_associates.verbatim_letter_context: 'I tent with James Lucas' / 'reduced to the ranks ... for being concerned in stealing rations' / 'James Lucas was reported killed ... shot through the head and arm'
confirmed_co_I_associates.record_match: LUCAS, JAMES.—Age 18; Co. I; corporal/returned-to-ranks (Aug 1 1863)/corporal again/sergeant June 1864; KILLED IN ACTION Oct 19 1864 at Cedar Creek, Va.
confirmed_co_I_associates.note: FATE THE LETTERS GOT WRONG — Charles hoped Lucas survived ('shot through head and arm'); the roster confirms he was killed. The ration-reduction matches 'returned to ranks Aug 1 1863.'

confirmed_co_I_associates.verbatim_letter_context: 'I tent with ... Sam Pelky' / 'Sergeant Pelkier (pronounced Pelky) from Corbeau of our town was shot through the leg'
confirmed_co_I_associates.record_match: PELTIER, SAMUEL.—Age 18; Co. I; sergeant Oct 18 1862; first sergeant Oct 1 1864; wounded Oct 19 1864 at Cedar Creek; discharged for wounds May 12 1865, Mower hospital, Philadelphia.
confirmed_co_I_associates.fate_from_record: wounded Cedar Creek (leg); discharged for wounds 1865
confirmed_co_I_associates.note: Wound matches Charles's letter exactly; phonetic 'Pelky' = Peltier.

confirmed_co_I_associates.name_as_written: Alek/Alex Douglas ('captured or killed ... by guerillas')
confirmed_co_I_associates.verbatim_letter_context: 'Alex Douglas has been missing about ten or twelve days ... taken prisoner by guerillas ... very much liked'
confirmed_co_I_associates.record_match: DOUGLASS, ALEXANDER J.—Age 18; enlisted Co. H; corporal Co. I Jan 1 1863; commissary sergeant May 9 1864; mustered out with regiment Oct 2 1865.
confirmed_co_I_associates.fate_from_record: SURVIVED — rose to commissary sergeant; mustered out 1865
confirmed_co_I_associates.note: FATE THE LETTERS COULDN'T KNOW (good news): the family feared him captured/killed by guerrillas Oct 1864; he survived the war.

confirmed_co_I_associates.record_match: TROMBLY, JR., BRUNO—Age 22; Co. I; corporal Oct 18 1862; discharged Jan 15 1864 to accept appointment as 2nd lieutenant, 20th Regiment U.S. Colored Troops.
confirmed_co_I_associates.fate_from_record: left to become an officer in the 20th U.S. Colored Troops
confirmed_co_I_associates.note: A notable trajectory: from Co. I corporal to USCT officer.

confirmed_co_I_associates.record_match: GOKEY, MOSES.—Age 33; Co. I; deserted Nov 19 1863.

confirmed_co_I_associates.name_as_written: 'Staats' (called out with Hubbell by Lieut. Knapp)
confirmed_co_I_associates.record_match: STATIA, PERRIN W.—Age 18; Co. I (Champlain); discharged for disability Nov 23 1863, Washington D.C.; also borne as Statie.
confirmed_co_I_associates.note: Probable match (Staats=Statia/Statie, the only Champlain Co. I fit) — flagged moderate-confidence, not forced.

confirmed_other_company_or_field_staff.name_as_written: Capt. Burdick ('Burdick 1st Lieut' → 'promoted to Captain' → 'has resigned')
confirmed_other_company_or_field_staff.record_match: BURDICK, MELANCTON S.—Age 44; 1st lieut. Co. G Oct 12 1862; captain May 1 1863; discharged for disability Aug 24 1863; also borne Birdsall.
confirmed_other_company_or_field_staff.note: Mustered Co. G but recurrent in Charles's letters; promotion/resignation dates match.

confirmed_other_company_or_field_staff.record_match: McMARTIN, DUNCAN.—Age 44; colonel Oct 18 1862; discharged for disability Apr 21 1863.
ARMSTRONG, THOMAS A.—Age 34; lieut.-colonel Oct 18 1862; discharged Feb 18 1863.

confirmed_other_company_or_field_staff.name_as_written: Lt. Col. Strain ('did he lose a leg?')
confirmed_other_company_or_field_staff.verbatim_letter_context: 'Did Lt. Colonel Strain lose a leg? Some say he did — others that he did not.'
confirmed_other_company_or_field_staff.record_match: STRAIN, ALEXANDER.—Age 31; captain Co. G Oct 8 1862; major May 1 1863; lieut.-colonel Dec 4 1863; wounded Oct 19 1864 at Cedar Creek; discharged for disability from wounds Jan 4 1865, Annapolis, Md.
confirmed_other_company_or_field_staff.fate_from_record: wounded (arm) Cedar Creek; discharged for wounds Jan 1865 — NO leg amputation recorded
confirmed_other_company_or_field_staff.note: ANSWERS the open question in the letters: Strain was wounded and discharged, but the roster records no amputation. He had gotten Charles his HQ/commissary clerk post.

confirmed_other_company_or_field_staff.name_as_written: De/Dr. Sweeney ('did all he could for James & I')
confirmed_other_company_or_field_staff.record_match: SWEENEY, JAMES.—Age 28; assistant surgeon June 1 1864; mustered out Oct 2 1865; prior service captain, 96th Infantry.
confirmed_other_company_or_field_staff.note: The surgeon who cared for Charles and James on the march.

honest_nulls_not_in_153rd.name: 'Welky'/'Welcky' (Charles's tentmate; lent him histories)
honest_nulls_not_in_153rd.note: NULL — no Welky/Welch/Welker in the 153rd; likely a phonetic French-Canadian Champlain surname not recoverable from spelling. Not forced.

honest_nulls_not_in_153rd.name: 'D. V. Savage'/'Savagham'
honest_nulls_not_in_153rd.note: NULL — no Savage/Savard/Savaria in the roster; possibly garbled French name or out-of-regiment. Not forced.

honest_nulls_not_in_153rd.name: 'Col. Sabastine[?]'
honest_nulls_not_in_153rd.note: NULL as written — probable garble of Col. Duncan McMartin (the only 153rd colonel of that period).

summary.co_I_officer_chain: Capt. Davis J. Rich (orig., disch. Nov 1863) -> Capt. John F. McGuire (1st Lt -> Capt., mustered out 1865); 2nd/1st Lt Charles L. Knapp (disch. Morganza May 1864).
fates_recovered: James Lucas — KILLED at Cedar Creek (letters thought he survived)
Alex Douglass — survived, rose to commissary sergeant (feared captured/killed)
Bruno Trombly — left to officer the 20th USCT
Lt. Col. Strain — wounded/discharged, no leg amputation (answers a letter's open question)
Sam Peltier — wounded Cedar Creek, discharged for wounds
summary.deadliest_day: Cedar Creek (Oct 19 1864) — for Charles's circle: Lucas killed; James Hubbell, Peltier, Lt. Col. Strain all wounded — exactly as Charles reported in LTR-1864-10-22-001.
